pull.title: feat(editor): alt-click to cycle the selection through overlapping elements
pull.body:
- Alt+click on the selected element (or group) selects the next one below it under the pointer, wrapping around to the topmost
  - a group is one stop; inside an edited group, it cycles through that group's elements only
  - also on the selected element's resize handles (where they're over the element)
- Alt+drag duplicates, and Alt+resize resizes from the center, only past a 10px drag threshold — a shorter alt-drag is an alt-click
- Alt+double-click no longer creates/edits text (except with the autoshape tool), so quick alt-clicks don't open the text editor
- Refactor: the selection tool's pointer handling moves out of App into `AppSelectionTool` (`app.selectionTool`): pointer down, the click selection of pointer up (`handleSelectionOnPointerUp`), and the transform handles (`maybeHandleResize` / `maybeHandleCrop`)
  - pure moves, verified mechanically — easiest to review commit by commit
- Tests for alt-click cycling, and for cropping by dragging a crop handle (wasn't covered through the pointer)

Why Alt and not Cmd/Ctrl: Cmd/Ctrl+click is deep select, and two quick Cmd+clicks are a Cmd+double-click (free text over a shape, arrow line editor, image crop).

Claude Opus 5.5 (xhigh)
